correctness.rationale: Exact induction/descent on max(a,b): diagonal and unit cases disposed of by F(t)=1 (mod t); for 2<=a<b let c=F(a)/b with 1<=c<a, then c|F(a) and a|F(c) from c^2F(b) congruent F(c) (mod a). Strictly smaller solution impossible. Euler-totient regrouping yields H(n)=n^-1 sum_{d|n} d phi(d) and the semiprime iff equivalence. Independent finite program tests all proper divisor partners for a<=5000, 200-by-200 pairs, and six product identities, but finite checks are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Closest full-text arXiv:2610.10572v1 Section 5 Proposition 1 provides only a quantitative upper bound for exactly the distinct-odd-prime two-cycle system, which does not imply emptiness. The proven theorem is an all-positive-integers no-two-cycle theorem and excludes squarefree semiprimes; the cited paper supplies no such exclusion. Searches of published research records, the OEIS sequence, and targeted external literature did not expose an equivalent or stronger result. Unindexed literature remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier proof of the same reciprocal-divisibility descent may exist.
Only the stated squarefree two-prime branch is eliminated; the general counting result and squared-prime cycle cases are not superseded.

value.rationale: The squarefree two-cycle system is a distinguished entire subcase of the source paper’s Section 5; proving its complete emptiness (even for composite operands) removes a natural structural branch rather than giving a small parameter improvement. It yields a new prime-support obstruction for the recently studied integrality set. The result does not claim a changed general asymptotic exponent or rule out higher-power cycles.
